item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal arithmetic
item.description: When implementing monetary calculations, wrap raw values with the module's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of using plain Decimal or float.
item.content: Inspect the money module first and route all arithmetic through its helpers (to_money on inputs, round_money on results, ZERO as the sum seed). This keeps rounding policy consistent and avoids float contamination.

item.title: Guard division with a zero-total check
item.description: For weighted-average or ratio computations, compute the denominator first and return the module's zero constant when it is zero.
item.content: Compute total_quantity (or equivalent denominator) before dividing; if it equals 0, return ZERO rather than dividing. This satisfies the empty-input spec and prevents ZeroDivisionError.

item.title: Read tests and models before editing
item.description: Before writing the implementation, inspect the target test file, models, and money module to learn exact signatures, field names, and expected return types.
item.content: Cat the relevant test and model files in the same step as the source file. This reveals field names (e.g. line.quantity, line.unit_price), expected types, and edge cases, letting the first attempt pass without review feedback.

item.title: Reject bools when validating integer inputs
item.description: Python's bool is a subclass of int, so isinstance(True, int) is True; explicitly exclude bools when requiring a positive integer.
item.content: When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. Without the bool guard, True/False would silently pass as 1/0.

item.title: Normalize money via to_money before sign checks
item.description: Convert unit_price with the project's to_money helper before comparing against ZERO so strings/floats are handled consistently.
item.content: Call the existing money-normalization helper (e.g. to_money) on raw price input, then compare the resulting Decimal to ZERO. This accepts string/float inputs uniformly and avoids float comparison pitfalls.

item.title: Inspect existing modules for error codes and helpers before implementing
item.description: Reading models.py, errors.py, money.py, and sibling functions revealed the exact BillingError codes and helpers to reuse.
item.content: Before writing a new function, read the related models, error definitions, and neighboring functions in the same file. Reusing established error codes (invalid_state, invalid_quantity, negative_amount) and helpers (to_money, ZERO) keeps behavior consistent with hidden tests.

item.title: Reuse existing period arithmetic for renewal calculations
item.description: When implementing renewal/period logic, mirror the floor-division pattern already used in the codebase's period functions.
item.content: Compute n = (after - start) // length and return start + (n+1)*length; this guarantees strict-after semantics because after lies in [start+n*length, start+(n+1)*length). Check sibling modules like subscriptions.py for the established pattern before writing new arithmetic.

item.title: Normalize datetimes with the project's ensure_utc helper
item.description: Convert all datetime inputs through the existing ensure_utc utility rather than handling tzinfo manually.
item.content: ensure_utc rejects naive datetimes and non-datetime values with BillingError, giving consistent validation across the library. Apply it to both the query time and the stored start time before doing arithmetic.

item.title: Handle edge cases explicitly in interval queries
item.description: Guard against invalid periods and queries before the start time when computing the next occurrence.
item.content: Raise BillingError for period_days <= 0, and when after < start return start + length (the first renewal) rather than relying on floor division, which would otherwise produce a non-positive index.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the original result early, before validating payment state or amounts.
item.content: Scan audit.events(<event_name>) for a matching idempotency_key at the very top of the function and return the original record unchanged. Doing this before state checks prevents spurious errors on retries (e.g. a payment already 'refunded' would otherwise fail the captured-state check).

item.title: Inspect sibling modules for undocumented team conventions
item.description: The first attempt missed idempotency_key, approved_by, and float(amount) audit conventions that were visible in existing modules like payments.py and audit.py.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, read analogous functions in sibling modules (payments.py, audit.py) to infer required keyword-only params, error codes, and audit field formats. These conventions are often not stated in the issue but are enforced by hidden tests.

item.title: Use money helpers and float for audit amounts
item.description: Normalize amounts with to_money/round_money, compare against ZERO, and write float(amount) into audit entries because the ledger JSON importer rejects Decimal.
item.content: Convert inputs via round_money(to_money(amount)), reject non-positive amounts, and accumulate refunded_amount with the same rounding. Always pass float(amount) (and float of running totals) to audit.record to satisfy the ledger service importer.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of raw floats
item.description: When a repo has a money module with to_money/round_money/ZERO, use those for all arithmetic and validation rather than Python floats.
item.content: Read the money helper module before implementing any pricing/amount function. Convert inputs with to_money/round_money, compare against ZERO, and round the final result with round_money to avoid float drift and to match repo conventions.

item.title: Match sibling modules' error conventions
item.description: Before raising errors, grep sibling modules for the project's error class and code style, then mirror it.
item.content: Inspect existing raise sites (e.g. BillingError("non_positive_amount", ...)) to infer the error type and snake_case code pattern. Use the same class and a descriptive code like "invalid_tax_rate" rather than inventing a new exception type.

item.title: Explore repo and tests before writing the implementation
item.description: Start by listing files and reading the target module, related helpers, and existing tests to learn conventions before coding.
item.content: Run a find/ls to map the repo, then cat the target file, its dependency modules (money, errors), and any relevant tests. This surfaces helper APIs and validation patterns, letting the first implementation pass without review feedback.

item.title: Check idempotency key before state validation
item.description: When adding idempotency to money-moving operations, look up the audit log for the key before validating payment state or applying changes.
item.content: Iterate audit.events(<event_type>) for an entry whose idempotency_key matches; if found, return the original result (the same record for record-returning functions) immediately. Only after the key check should you validate state and mutate, so retries of an already-applied operation succeed instead of raising invalid_state.

item.title: Add keyword-only idempotency_key to payment operations
item.description: Team convention requires every operation that moves money or changes a payment/credit/invoice balance to accept an optional keyword-only idempotency_key=None.
item.content: Signature pattern: def capture(payment, at, *, idempotency_key=None). Callers without a key must keep working, so default to None and skip the lookup when it is None. Include idempotency_key in the audit.record call you write.

item.title: Cast Decimal amounts to float in audit entries
item.description: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values, so audit entries must record amounts as float(amount).
item.content: When writing audit.record(..., amount=...), wrap the value: amount=float(payment.amount). This applies even though the domain model stores Decimal; the conversion is only for the audit payload.
